lesson.text: Quick memory: in a budget, what comes after needs? (Saving.) Where can savings go? Under a bed, in a money box, or into a bank. Today: what banks do, and how interest makes savings grow.

A bank keeps people's money safe in accounts. It lets them pay by card or phone, as you saw in grade 4, and lends money to people and businesses. Banks keep a record of every coin that goes in and out.
Banks do not keep all the money in a vault. They lend much of it to others, who pay extra, called interest, for borrowing it. Part of that interest is paid back to the savers.
Interest is money a bank pays you for keeping your savings there. It is given as a percentage: 5% a year means 5 gold for every 100 gold saved, each year.
Tilly saves 300 gold at 5% a year. 300 gold is 3 hundreds, and each hundred earns 5 gold: 3 × 5 = 15 gold. After a year she has 300 + 15 = 315 gold, without doing any work.

With simple interest, the bank pays the same each year, on the money first saved: 15 gold a year for 4 years is 15 × 4 = 60 gold. Many banks pay interest on the interest too, called compound interest: you will meet it next year.
Keep your bank details private, like a password; your card's PIN is only for you. A real bank never asks for your password in a message. If something seems odd, tell a grown-up.
Try it in the world: set up a bank chest in your base with a sign: for every 10 gold kept there a whole week, add 1 gold of interest. Watch your savings grow. Next: borrowing and paying back.

choices: money a bank pays you for saving
exercises.explain: Interest is money the bank pays you for keeping your savings there.

exercises.prompt: Banks lend out some of the money people save.
exercises.hint: Where does a bank get money to lend?
exercises.explain: True: banks lend out much of the money savers keep there.

exercises.prompt: 5% a year means how much for every 100 gold saved?
exercises.explain: 5 gold for every 100 gold, each year.

exercises.prompt: It is fine to tell a friend your bank password.
exercises.explain: False: keep it private, like your PIN.

exercises.prompt: Which is a safe place for savings that can earn interest?
exercises.explain: A bank account keeps money safe and can pay interest.

exercises.prompt: Zara saves 400 gold at 5% a year. How much interest does she earn in one year?
exercises.hint: 5 gold for every 100 gold. How many hundreds?

exercises.prompt: Bram saves 200 gold at 3% a year. How much is in his account after one year?
exercises.hint: Find the interest, then add it to the savings.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
matches: a secret number for a card
extra paid when money is lent
your money's record at a bank
exercises.hint: Which one must you keep secret?
exercises.explain: Income: money in. Interest: extra paid. Account: your record. PIN: your secret number.

exercises.prompt: Why does a bank pay interest to savers?
exercises.hint: Where does the bank's money come from?
choices: it lends their money and earns interest
exercises.explain: The bank lends savers' money to borrowers and shares part of the interest with the savers.

exercises.prompt: At 10% a year, 100 gold earns 10 gold of interest in a year.
Mimi saves 500 gold at 4% simple interest. How much interest does she earn in 3 years?
exercises.hint: Work out one year first, then times it by 3.
exercises.explain: 500 gold is 5 hundreds: 5 × 4 = 20 gold a year. 20 × 3 = 60 gold.

exercises.prompt: Bank A pays 2% a year and Bank B pays 5% a year. Where do savings grow faster?
exercises.hint: Which pays more gold for every 100?
exercises.explain: Bank B: 5 gold for every 100 instead of 2.

exercises.prompt: Tilly had 600 gold. After one year the bank added 18 gold. What percentage interest was that?
exercises.explain: 600 gold is 6 hundreds. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 gold for every 100: 3%.

exercises.prompt: A message says it is from your bank and asks for your password. What do you do?
exercises.hint: Would a real bank ask for your password?
choices: don't reply, and tell a grown-up
exercises.explain: A real bank never asks for your password in a message. Don't reply, and tell a grown-up.

exercises.prompt: Compound interest pays interest on the interest too.
exercises.hint: Next year you will meet it.
exercises.explain: True: with compound interest, last year's interest earns interest too.
